text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Three years after selling its Asian assets, Westpac Banking Corp will again move into the region and hopes to poach corporate customers with a new agreement with Standard Chartered Bank of the United Kingdom. The move will see Standard offer Westpac's coporate customers banking services through its extensive network in Asia. Page 1.

In a busy day for gold stocks, the share price of Perth-based junior Helix Resources NL doubled to A$3.70 yesterday after the release of strong drilling results from a gold discovery in the Gawler Craton in South Australia. Helix chairman Robert Mosig sad last night the discovery sends a message throughout the world to "get in there and get some of the action". Page 1.

According to a study of board remuneration and practice conducted by remuneration consultancy Cullen Egan Dell, the mid-range remuneration for chairmen is now about A$60,000, Australian boards are paying more attention to their shareholders and to corporae governance issues and more women are being admitted to the boardroom. Released at a function held yesterday by the Chartered Institute of Company Secretaries in Australia, the survey covered 180 organisations. Page 2.

A bid of over A$450 million is expected to be placed by mining giant Placer Pacific on Highlands Gold, following an A$85 million sharemarket raid through Macquarie Equities late yesterday. The raid netted Placer 20 percent of Highlands Gold, which has a interest in the massive Porgera gold deposit in Papua New Guinea. Page 23.

Lend Lease and a joint venture between Commonwealth Bank Financial Services and Westfield Holdings are the two buyers left in the final stages of the race for Commonwealth Funds Management. As the deadline for final bids closed last Friday, it is believed AMP Society and the ANZ Bank had quit as potential buyers. Page 23.

RTZ-CRA subsidiary Comalco Ltd had decided to shut down its unsuccessful kaolin business and will instead focus on its large Weipa bauxite mining operation in north Queensland and a possible A$1 billion alumina refinery. Comalco said the exit from its koalin business would result in a net abnormal loss of up to A$40 million. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The release of promising drill results from Helix Resources NL's 100 percent owned Tunkillia prospect at Lake Everard in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia saw shares in the company rise to a high of A$3.65 yesterday, up A$1.85. The rise saw Helix's market capitalisation more than double to A$156 million. Page 25.

Australia's big banks and leading life insurers have been criticised by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission over their approach to the Wallis banking inquiry, which the ACCC says is an attempt to secure a captive regulator for the financial sector. The interim report of the Wallis inquiry is due for release today. Page 25.

In an attempt to ensure Australia is still a viable option for its proposed A$1 billion alumina refinery, Comalco Ltd will axe up to 150 jobs at its Weipa minerals and alumina operation in Queensland and close its loss-making kaolin mine. The Comalco board will soon look at plans for the alumina refinery, which will be in either Gladstone, Queensland, or Sarawak, Malaysia, and will then recommend a site to its major shareholder RTZ-CRA. Page 25.

Following the move by an unidentified buyer to grab 33.3 percent of Papua New Guinea-based miner Highlands Gold Ltd, a A$480 million takeover offer of the company is expected to be announced today. The offer, at 85 cents a share, is expected to come from local gold heavyweight Placer Pacific Ltd, or a large offshore base-metal producer. Page 25.

A survey by remuneration consultant Cullen Egan Dell, conducted on behalf of the Chartered Institute of Company Secretaries in Australia, has found company directors continue to win wage rises far in excess of those claimed by average workers. The survey also found that just five per cent of companies have a formal review procedure to determine their directors' fees. Page 25.

The Perpetual Funds Management's Savings Pulse survey has found that people are saving less than they were a year ago, with the mean level of monthly savings falling from A$383 to A$267 during the 12 months to November. The survey also found people are putting their money into more conservative investment products. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Papua New Guinea goldminer Highlands Gold is under attack from Canadian mining group Placer Dome, which spent up to A$140 million in share market raid yesterday to grab a controlling shareholding. Highlands owns a 25 per cent stake in the one million ounces-a-year Porgera gold mine in partnership with Placer's Australian offshoot Placer Pacific, and RGC and the Papua New Guinea Government. Page 25.

Westpac Banking Corp group executive of institutional and international banking David Morgan has brokered a deal with Standard Chartered Bank to share customers and banking facilities in the Asian and Australian markets. The move sees a return to the international scene for Westpac, which recently sold A$11 billion of foreign assets. Page 25.

BHP and other major Australian miners look set to end the year on a higher note after evidence of dwindling stockpiles on the London Metal Exchange saw another jump in the world copper price. While the metal is at its best price since June 2, the stockmaket is remaining cool. Page 25.

In an attempt to stem its share of losses in the Australian pay TV industry, pay TV group Optus Vision will raise prices by between 15 and 20 per cent. The losses are estimated at a total of A$600 million last financial year. Optus Vision itself booked loss of about A$159 million for 1995-96. Page 25.

The release today of the Wallis Inquiry discussion paper into Australia's financial system has many industry observers feeling a cooling in the Federal Government's attitude towards a radical overhaul of the financial system, including reduced regulatory power for the Reserve Bank and the allowance of mergers between the major banks and insurance companies, as it realises this does not make political sense. Page 27.

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp believes the Federal Government's formula for calculating landing charges at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports after privatisation, guarantees the charges will fall in real terms for five years and could lead to lower air fares. Page 27.
THE AGE

Helix Resources NL's share price doubled to A$3.70 yesterday, on the back of further impressive results from a line of holes drilled 100 metres to the east of the initial discovery holes at its Tunkillia prospect. The Helix results confirmed Gawler Crato as a "hot" new area for gold exploration and boosted the share prices of other companies with ground in the region. Page B1.

The announcement yesterday by Westpac that it had formed an alliance in Asia with United Kingdom-based Standard Chartered Bank, indicating the possibility of a merger, has revealed changes in the bank's Asian strategy. The move will centre on Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Hong Kong and Singapore, where Standard Chartered operates 160 branches, and will then lead to China and Vietnam. Page B1.

A boardroom survey of around 200 Australian companies by management consulting firm Cullen Egan Dell has found Australian companies are more sensitive than ever to pressure from shareholders and corporate governance issues. The survey found changing patterns of appointment, payment and performance measurement. Page B1.

After consulting the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, the Federal Government announced yesterday it had finalised the method of calculating landing charges at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports after they are privatised. The charges are based on potential for productivity improvements and traffic growth and according to Transport Minister John Sharp, they will fall for five years and could lead to lower air fares. Page B3.

Dairy products company Tatura Milk Industries last night won The Age/Dun Bradstreet Grand Champion's award after earlier winning the prize in the rural category. Tatura will receive A$25,000 of Dun & Bradstreet's accounting products and services on top of its A$2500 prize as the rural category winner. Page B3.

After questioning 1200 Australian small businesses, the Yellow Pages Small Business Index revealed yesterday that 62 per cent of small businesses believe the economy has stalled and 18 per cent believe it is in recession. The index showed an overall nineper cent rise in sales during the three months ending in October, but the wholesale-retail sector showed more falls in sales than rises, while the building and construction sector enjoyed a 10 per cent net sales increase. Page B3.
